_comment: Every variable the website and the model service read. `name` must match .env.example (checked), unless `notInExample` gives the reason it is deliberately absent. readBy: Node, Python or both.

precedence.intro: Both programs read the same settings in the same order. The first one that has a value wins.

steps.title: The real environment
steps.text: A variable set in the terminal (export NAME=value) or by the host. It always wins over the file, so a deployment can override .env without editing it.

steps.title: The env file
steps.text: The file named by TERUCON_ENV_FILE, otherwise .env next to package.json. It is re-read whenever it changes: save it and reload the page. Only HOST, PORT and the MODEL_* settings need a restart.

steps.title: The built-in default
steps.text: What the column below shows. A blank value in the file counts as not set.

precedence.envFileNote: The one way to point both programs at a different file (a relative path is relative to the project folder). Every test sets it, together with an explicit environment, so no test can ever read your real .env or call real Google. Express passes it on to the model service it starts.

groups.title: Where the website listens
groups.blurb: Read by Express. HOST and PORT need a restart.

groups.title: Google Cloud
groups.blurb: Pick one way to sign in. Read by both programs, because each has its own Google client.

groups.title: Model names
groups.blurb: Blank means the Design Studio's own defaults. A value here wins over the Studio's settings.

groups.title: How surfaces are found
groups.blurb: Shown to the Studio by /api/config and used by the model service.

groups.title: SAM (optional)
groups.blurb: Sharper edges and the Pick tool. Everything works with SAM off.

groups.title: The model service
groups.blurb: How Express starts and talks to the Python service.

vars.name: HOST
vars.effect: Where Express listens. 127.0.0.1 means only this computer. 0.0.0.0 exposes the server (and your Google credentials) to the network: use it only on a trusted network, and set SAM_SERVER_KEY if you serve SAM.

vars.name: PORT
vars.effect: The port Express listens on. If it is taken, the server says so and exits.

vars.name: ALLOWED_HOSTS
vars.effect: Extra host names the site may be opened under (comma separated), for when it is served from a domain. Any other Host header is refused with 421.

vars.name: GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
vars.effect: Option A, recommended: the whole service-account key on one line inside single quotes (raw JSON, or base64 of it). Vertex AI with this key. The key's token_uri must be googleapis.com.

vars.name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
vars.effect: Instead of pasting the key: the path to the key file (absolute, or relative to the project folder). The path is not secret; the file is.

vars.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
vars.effect: The project id, for example my-project-123. A key pasted here by mistake still works, with a warning to move it.

vars.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION
vars.effect: Vertex AI location. global is right for the Nano Banana models; others: us-central1, asia-south1.

vars.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
vars.effect: Option B: a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio. Simpler, but it is the Gemini API rather than your Cloud project. Leave option A blank to use it.

vars.name: GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI
vars.effect: true uses Vertex AI (service account, or application default credentials); false uses the API key. Blank picks whichever is configured.

vars.name: SWATCHROOM_IMAGE_MODEL
vars.effect: The render model ("Nano Banana"). Passed to the Studio through /api/config. If it is not available to the project, a neighbouring model is tried.

vars.name: SWATCHROOM_DETECT_MODEL
vars.effect: The model that finds and outlines surfaces; needs structured output and vision. Python uses it for detection; the Studio shows it. This is also where a fine-tuned Gemini endpoint name would go.

vars.name: SWATCHROOM_MASK_MODEL
vars.effect: Optional pixel-mask model for the older Gemini-only engine. gemini-2.5-flash retires on Vertex AI on 20 October 2026.

vars.name: SWATCHROOM_INSIGHT_MODEL
vars.effect: Quantity and material take-off estimates.

vars.name: SEGMENTATION_ENGINE
vars.effect: auto: Gemini names the surfaces, edge snapping aligns them, SAM corrects first if it is on, and the in-browser parser is the fallback. scene: only the in-browser parser (no Google, works offline). gemini: only Gemini in the browser (the old engine).

vars.name: EDGE_REFINE
vars.effect: Snap the outlines (and SAM's edges) onto the photo's real edges.

vars.name: EDGE_METHOD
vars.effect: contour slides each boundary onto the nearest convincing edge, paying for every pixel it moves (recommended). watershed is the earlier method, kept as a fallback.

vars.name: ANALYSIS_MAX_SIDE
vars.effect: Detection resolution in pixels (512 to 3072). Higher means finer edges and a slower scan.

vars.name: SAM_ENABLED
vars.effect: Turns SAM on. Needs pip install -r model/requirements-sam.txt for the local backends; the model (about 180 MB) downloads on first use.

vars.name: SAM_BACKEND
vars.effect: auto | sam2 | sam | sam3 | remote. auto chooses remote if SAM_REMOTE_URL is set, else sam3 if SAM_CHECKPOINT is set, else sam2.

vars.name: SAM_MODEL_ID
vars.effect: Which Hugging Face model. tiny is fastest; base-plus and large are sharper but slower.

vars.name: SAM_DEVICE
vars.effect: auto | cpu | cuda | mps.

vars.name: SAM_PRELOAD
vars.effect: Load the model as soon as the service starts, so the first scan does not wait.

vars.name: HF_TOKEN
vars.effect: A Hugging Face token, needed only for gated models such as facebook/sam3.

vars.name: SAM_CHECKPOINT
vars.effect: SAM 3 on a GPU machine: the path to sam3.pt.

vars.name: SAM_REPO_DIR
vars.effect: SAM 3: the folder of the cloned sam3 package.

vars.name: SAM_REMOTE_URL
vars.effect: Use a SAM server running somewhere else (a GPU box, Kaggle, Colab). Include /sam or /api/sam in the address. Any server that answers /health, /segment and /refine works.

vars.name: SAM_REMOTE_KEY
vars.effect: The key to send to that remote server.

vars.name: SAM_REMOTE_AUTH_HEADER
vars.effect: bearer or x-api-key: how the remote key is sent.

vars.name: SAM_SERVER_KEY
vars.effect: On the GPU machine: require this key (x-api-key or Bearer) for SAM requests. Use the same value as SAM_REMOTE_KEY on the machine that calls it.

vars.name: SAM_MAX_SIDE
vars.notInExample: tuning knob that was never in the template
vars.effect: Longest side, in pixels, that SAM sees (256 to 2048).

vars.name: TERUCON_ENV_FILE
vars.effect: Path of the env file for both programs. Relative paths are relative to the project folder. Express passes it to the model service. Tests always set it.
vars.notInExample: it chooses the file, so it cannot live inside it; set it in the real environment

vars.name: MODEL_SERVICE
vars.effect: auto starts the Python service as a child process; external uses MODEL_SERVICE_URL and starts nothing; off means no model service (the Studio uses its in-browser parser).

vars.name: MODEL_SERVICE_URL
vars.effect: Base URL of a service you run yourself, for example http://127.0.0.1:8081. Only used with MODEL_SERVICE=external.

vars.name: MODEL_SERVICE_KEY
vars.effect: Shared secret. Express sends it as X-Terucon-Model-Key; a service that has one refuses requests without it. In auto mode Express generates one for each run and hands it to the child.

vars.name: MODEL_HOST
vars.effect: Where the service listens when you run it yourself.

vars.name: MODEL_PORT
vars.effect: The service's port. 0 lets the system choose a free one; Express always starts the child with 0 and reads the real port from its READY line.

vars.name: MODEL_PARENT_PID
vars.effect: When set, the service exits within about 3 seconds of that process disappearing, so a website killed with kill -9 leaves no orphan behind.
vars.notInExample: set by Express for the service it starts, not by hand

vars.name: MODEL_START_TIMEOUT
vars.effect: Seconds Express waits for the service's READY line. If it takes longer the service is reported unavailable (with that reason) and not restarted in a loop.

vars.name: PYTHON
vars.effect: The interpreter for the service. When set it is the only one tried. Otherwise, in order: model/.venv, .venv, python3, python (Windows: Scripts\python.exe, py -3). One is accepted only if flask, numpy, PIL, cv2, requests and google.auth import.

vars.name: TERUCON_ALLOW_CUSTOM_GOOGLE_ENDPOINTS
vars.notInExample: test-only; deliberately not offered in the template
vars.effect: Lets a service-account key name a token endpoint outside googleapis.com. Used by tests against a fake Google. Never set it on a real deployment.

vars.name: TERUCON_VERTEX_API_BASE
vars.notInExample: test-only; deliberately not offered in the template
vars.effect: Points Vertex calls at a local fake. Honoured only when TERUCON_ALLOW_CUSTOM_GOOGLE_ENDPOINTS is true.

notes: Express parses every SAM_* variable too, so its start-up banner can say what SAM is set to, but only SAM_ENABLED and SAM_SERVER_KEY change what Express does. "Read by" names who acts on a variable.

A key pasted into the wrong variable, invalid JSON, a key whose token_uri is not Google's, a model name your project cannot use, and a wrong clock are all detected and explained; the Studio shows the reason.

The browser never receives a value from this table. /api/config returns only the safe summary: whether Google is configured, its mode, the project id and location, the model names, the segmentation settings, and the SAM and model-service state.
